lines.text: The Moon is running away from us.
And how we know is even stranger.
Every year, it drifts about three point eight centimeters farther away.
lines.caption: Every year, it drifts about 3.8 cm farther away.

lines.text: That's roughly as fast as your fingernails grow.
Earth's ocean tides are slowly nudging it outward.
We know because Apollo astronauts left mirrors on the Moon, and scientists still fire lasers at them.
The beam spreads so wide, sometimes just one photon comes back every few seconds.
Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
